Hi everyone! My name is Ruth Plümer, I am a Bachelor student at the University of Bonn. Last year, I took Floris van Doorn's course "Formalizing Mathematics in Lean" and I'm currently writing my Bachelor thesis on a Lean topic as well. I am interested in Mathematical Logic, specifically Model Theory. Some of you might already have seen some of my Lean-related questions I asked on here before.

Today, I opened my first pull request in mathlib in order to add something that annoyed me when working on my thesis. I noticed that in Mathlib.ModelTheory.Semantics, there are a lot of simp theorems like FirstOrder.Language.BoundedFormula.realize_sup and FirstOrder.Language.Formula.realize_sup, respectively, that describe how Boolean operations can be "pulled out" of the interpretation, but for Sentences, there is only FirstOrder.Language.Sentence.realize_not, which results in the fact that simp cannot prove a statement like 

M \vDash (\phi \inf \psi) \iff (M \vDash \phi \and M \vDash \psi)

where \phi and psi are of the type L.Sentence and M is an L.Structure, so I added new simp theorems Sentence.realize_bot, Sentence.realize_top, Sentence.realize_inf, Sentence.realize_sup, Sentence.realize_imp and Sentence.realize_iff that are analogous to Sentence.realize_not.

I hope that this is a useful contribution and apologize if the non-existence of these theorems was intended.
Welcome! I don't know enough model theory to judge, but this area in mathlib is definitely under-developed. To cross-reference, your PR is #39996.
